newsitem.title: FINLAND: ETLA SEES INCREASING HOUSEHOLD CREDIT DEMAND 1997.
newsitem.headline: ETLA SEES INCREASING HOUSEHOLD CREDIT DEMAND 1997.

text.p: Household demand for housing loans will grow further next year due to lower interest rates and rising disposable income, the Research Institute of the Finnish Economy (ETLA) said in a report received on Thursday.
"The decline in real interest rates and rise in disposable real income will fuel the credit demand of households next year," ETLA said in the report dated November 27.

It said household housing loan demand had turned suddenly this year. "The demand for new credit has picked up and the amount of outstanding housing loans has started to rise after a four-year decline," ETLA said.

"The demand for housing loans is bolstered also by the fact that housing prices have started to rise," it said, adding: "A rise in housing prices like that witnessed in the end of the 1980s is nevertheless not anticipated."
Despite increasing demand for housing loans, banks were not in for massive credit extension growth, ETLA said.

"There are ... no signs of an upswing in the demand for consumer and other loans to households. The forecast for housing loans appears to be underestimated while the demand for consumer and other loans has been overestimated," it said.
On balance, ETLA said the projections for the overall credit demand of households seemed to be on target.
